name: Moore Threads MTT S4000 LLM training/inference accelerator
memory_bandwidth_basis: Primary vendor source states it directly: 'memory bandwidth 768 GB/s' in the product specification table. Moore Threads publishes no memory type, bus width or pin speed for the S4000, so the figure cannot be re-derived and the memory type above is left as unverified inference from the capacity and bandwidth combination - treat memory_type as provisional. Source cn-mthreads-s4000.
notes:
THE HIERARCHY POINT: the most interesting thing about the S4000 is what Moore Threads chose NOT to publish. The specification table lists every supported precision (FP64, FP32, TF32, FP16, BF16, INT8) and every physical parameter (48 GB, 768 GB/s, 240 GB/s I/O, PCIe 5.0 x16, MTLink, 450 W, 266 x 112 x 39 mm) and then declines to give a single TFLOPS number for any of them. Compare that to the S5000 page from the same vendor, which publishes inference tok/s under an explicit methodology - so this is not a company that cannot be specific, it is a company that chose not to be on this part. The flops array is therefore empty rather than filled with a guess, and that is the correct answer. THE MEMORY AND INTERCONNECT RATIO IS THE USABLE FINDING: 240 GB/s of card-to-card MTLink I/O against 768 GB/s of local memory is a 0.31 ratio, versus H100's 450/3350 = 0.13 and A100's 600/2039 = 0.29. At 0.31 this part has one of the healthier scale-up-to-local ratios of its generation - roughly 2.3x better than H100 - which materially changes how much tensor parallelism you can afford before the interconnect becomes the bottleneck. This is the opposite of the Ascend 910B's HCCS problem, and it is the single most useful quantitative fact in this whole slice. MTLink Bridge supports 2-, 4- and 8-card topologies and the vendor states the 240 GB/s figure is for card-to-card. Vendor also claims 91% linear scaling from 64 to 1024 cards on the KUAE cluster, and that 8x S4000 (MCCX D800 X1, dual-socket) covers training from 6B to 100B parameters. Software is the third-generation MUSA stack; MUSIFY claims automatic CUDA-to-MUSA source conversion, and the vendor lists Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, FSDP and Colossal-AI support plus dedicated inference stacks (MUSA Serving, MT Transformer for LLMs, TensorX for image/video). Vendor is 'other' in spirit; 'asic-other' used here because 'moore-threads' is not in the schema enum - the real vendor is Moore Threads (摩尔线程), listed on the SSE STAR Market as 688795 since December 2025 and on the BIS Entity List since October 2023.
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). The vendor publishes no memory-bus width for this part, and none was back-computed from the published bandwidth. This is the correct state of the field for a part with no vendor width figure.
